dish: the seasonal Lorraine tasting menus (incl. a menu dedicated to lobster) behind the glass-walled kitchen
n: Transparence — La Table de Patrick Fréchin
w: A MICHELIN-starred table a few steps from Place Stanislas on the pedestrian rue Stanislas, where 'transparency' is literal — you watch chef Patrick Fréchin work through a glass partition. Beautifully plated seasonal menus (including one built around lobster); one Michelin star, recognised by Gault&Millau.

dish: creative seasonal brasserie cooking — mushroom brioche, stuffed pollock, everything (bread, brioche, pickles, hydromel) made in-house
address: Place du Roi George, 57000 Metz, France
w: Opened March 2024 in central Metz by Olivier Rasia with pastry-trained chef Claire Arthaud (ex-Le Grand Restaurant de Jean-François Piège, ex-Toya alongside Loïc Villemin), the 11 fuses gastronomy and art de vivre. The card is rewritten every three weeks; a fast-rising favourite hailed by Gilles Pudlowski and France Bleu and listed by Gault&Millau.

dish: cave-aged Lorraine & French cheeses (munster, comté, raclette) — affineur boards
w: One of France's oldest and largest cheese-ageing houses, seven generations of maîtres fromagers-affineurs in Nancy's Ville-Vieille, ripening over 100 cheeses in their own caves — with an adjoining restaurant at 99 Grande Rue. A Gault&Millau-listed artisan and a Lorraine institution for munster and mountain cheeses.

dish: Lorraine classics — baeckeoffe au foie gras, poularde aux morilles, game and truffle in winter
w: In an old de Ligneville mansion on the Grande Rue, chef Patrick Tanésy keeps Lorraine's culinary traditions alive — bistrot by day, refined tasting menus by night. Gault&Millau-listed and named Bistrot of the Year 2007 by the Pudlowski guide; a beloved guardian of the region's table.

dish: mirabelle de Lorraine eau-de-vie and liqueurs (plus a mirabelle museum & tasting)
n: Maison de la Mirabelle — Distillerie Grallet-Dupic
address: 16 Rue du Capitaine Durand, 54290 Rozelieures, France
w: A family distillery amid the plum orchards of Rozelieures showcasing Lorraine's golden fruit: an educational visit through the history and cultivation of the mirabelle, an alambic hall with a sound-and-light show, and a tasting room of mirabelle eau-de-vie, liqueurs and specialities. The definitive place to taste Lorraine's signature spirit.

dish: contemporary market cuisine with Italian & Japanese accents on Pays-de-Bitche produce
w: Below the great citadelle of Bitche, self-taught chef Lutz Janisch cooks a generous, inventive cuisine — French base, Italian and Japanese touches, local product — that made Le Strasbourg the reference table of the northern Moselle. Listed by the MICHELIN Guide and Gault&Millau, with rooms above.

dish: market-fresh Lorraine terroir menu from short supply chains and reasoned agriculture
w: A stone's throw from Place Stanislas, young chef Martin Debuiche cooks a market-driven score anchored in Lorraine terroir, in a wood-and-greenery room evoking fields — hence the name Racine. Listed by the MICHELIN Guide and praised by Le Fooding and Zut Magazine.

dish: refined seasonal gastronomy (the house glace Plombières a Lorraine classic)
address: 2 Quartier de la Gare, 57200 Wœlfling-lès-Sarreguemines, France
w: Between Sarreguemines and Bitche, in an imposing 1950s building at the forest's edge, chef Julien Dimofski — Gault&Millau's Trophée Grand de Demain 2017 — cooks a clean, precise, flavour-forward gastronomy. Listed by the MICHELIN Guide and Gault&Millau, with a garden for summer service.

dish: historic 18th-century Stanislas-era cuisine — Lorraine, Polish and royal-table dishes
n: À la Table du Bon Roi Stanislas
w: An original 2002 concept in the Ville-Vieille recreating the table of Stanislas Leszczyński — Lorraine, Polish and 18th-century French specialities tied to the deposed Polish king turned Duke of Lorraine. Gault&Millau-listed and long a Nancy favourite; a delicious way into the city's history.

dish: the Saint-Epvre (almond-meringue, nougatine, vanilla cream) and macarons de Nancy
w: By the Saint-Epvre basilica in the old town, the house of Jean-François Adam (a Lorraine pâtisserie since 1883) keeps the trademarked Saint-Epvre cake — two almond-meringue discs, vanilla buttercream and crushed nougatine, registered since 1907 — alongside macarons de Nancy and bergamot sweets. Bearer of the 'Nancy Passions Sucrées' label.

dish: house antipasti, mushroom ravioli with parmesan crisp, Neapolitan pizza
w: A chic bistronomic Italian a stone's throw from Place Stanislas — restaurant, wine cellar and fine-food shop in one — pouring carefully sourced Italian product into antipasti, fresh pasta and Neapolitan pizza. A Gault&Millau-selected Nancy address.

dish: medal-winning breads and the Galette des Rois (bronze, Meilleure Boulangerie de France 2024)
w: A Metz boulangerie baking since 1932 — sourdough, organic and cereal breads and traditional baguettes — with a wall of medals: repeated Moselle 'best puff-pastry galette' wins, Grand Est gold (2019, 2022) and a bronze for Best Galette of France on TV's La Meilleure Boulangerie de France 2024. Championed by Gilles Pudlowski and the Inspire Metz tourist office.

dish: neo-Lorraine bistronomy under the vaults of the 1559 royal victualling store
w: Beneath the centuries-old vaults of a 16th-century former royal food store (now the La Citadelle MGallery hotel), La Réserve serves a generous neo-Lorraine bistronomy that celebrates local producers and seasonal vegetables. Listed by the MICHELIN Guide (a toque at Gault&Millau) and the Inspire Metz office.

dish: inventive French seasonal cuisine from fresh local product
w: A small, warm Thionville table (about 40 covers, half on the terrace) where Didier and Barbara Delanaux cook an inventive cuisine in the purest respect of French tradition, seasonal and market-led. Gault&Millau-rated and carried by the Moselle and Thionville tourist offices.

dish: regional Lorraine gastronomy in a Relais & Châteaux manor
n: Le Manoir du Soldat (ex-Au Soldat de l'An II)
w: The renowned Phalsbourg manor created by Georges Schmitt — a subtly restored old barn of stone, beams and fine porcelain — reborn as Le Manoir du Soldat under chef Philippe Ghiloni, now serving an accessible regional gastronomy. A MICHELIN-Guide address long followed by critic Gilles Pudlowski and Les Nouvelles Gastronomiques.

dish: natural-wine glasses with small plates on the Outre-Seille terraces
w: A very cosy wine bar on rue Sainte-Marie — one of the Outre-Seille lanes where Messins gather every evening for a glass on the terrace. Singled out by Gault&Millau as one of the 'ten addresses that make Metz'.

dish: house-roasted specialty coffee, plus bagels and house pastries
w: An independent specialty coffee shop and roaster on rue Gambetta, opened 2017 and billed as the Grand Est's largest (270 m2), roasting its own beans in the room before you. A genuine third-wave destination flagged by the specialty-coffee press and Supermiro.

dish: the authentic madeleines de Commercy (shell-shaped butter cakes)
n: La Boîte à Madeleines — Madeleines Zins
w: A Commercy madeleinerie since 1951 perpetuating the true madeleine de Commercy — Lorraine's emblematic shell-shaped little cake — with a workshop you can tour, a boutique and a summer tea-room terrace. One of the last houses keeping the town's Proustian speciality alive.
